title: Solar Radiation Storm (SPE)
first_screen_message: Move to the shielded storm shelter immediately. Countdown to peak proton arrival: 05:45:00 — suspend all EVAs and check personal dosimeter.
steps: Suspend any planned or active EVA and close viewport shutters.
Move all crew to the water/polyethylene-shielded storm shelter module.
Verify each crew member's personal dosimeter is powered and synced; compare today's dose + mission cumulative dose against NASA's 600 mSv career limit.
Log shelter entry time and verify cabin CO2 scrubber and potable water supply inside the shielded zone.
Remain sheltered until NOAA SWPC / onboard particle flux returns below storm threshold.
why_this_happens: Solar Particle Events eject high-energy protons that acutely raise radiation dose, suppressing radio-sensitive lymphocytes and increasing oxidative and vascular strain.
when_to_escalate: Escalate to Mission Control & Flight Surgeon immediately if acute daily dose exceeds 10 mSv, shelter shielding is compromised, or any crew member reports nausea, fatigue, or prodromal symptoms.
disclaimer: Simulated protocol for demo. Real procedures come from the flight surgeon.

title: Fainting / Dizziness (Orthostatic / Fluid Shift)
first_screen_message: Secure the crew member in a safe floating/seated strap position, check airway and pulse, and begin guided oral rehydration + lower-body compression check.
steps: Stabilize the crew member so they cannot drift into hardware; keep head neutral and airway clear.
Check manual radial/carotid pulse and wearable RHR, then measure SpO2 and blood pressure (cuff at heart level).
Compare blood pressure to the astronaut's in-flight personal baseline (microgravity lowers BP ~10 mmHg).
Offer 500 mL electrolyte fluid if alert and able to swallow; check cabin CO2 for hypercapnia.
Monitor vitals every 5 minutes for 30 minutes and log episode in Emergency Events.
why_this_happens: Microgravity shifts blood headward and reduces plasma volume; dehydration, CO2 buildup, or transition back toward gravity/LBNP can trigger sudden lightheadedness or presyncope.
when_to_escalate: Escalate immediately if unresponsive > 30 s, systolic BP drops > 20 mmHg below personal in-flight baseline, SpO2 < 92%, or dizziness recurs.
disclaimer: Simulated protocol for demo. Real procedures come from the flight surgeon.

title: Chest Pain / Acute Cardiac Symptoms
first_screen_message: Stop all physical exertion immediately. Strap crew member safely, attach chest ECG / wearable + pulse oximeter, and alert the Flight Surgeon.
steps: Halt exercise or EVA prep immediately and restrain the crew member comfortably in neutral posture.
Measure resting heart rate, SpO2, and bilateral blood pressure (2 readings 1 min apart); verify chest ECG lead contact.
Ask about pain character, radiation to arm/jaw, shortness of breath, nausea, or diaphoresis.
Keep emergency medical kit and AED staged nearby in microgravity restraint straps.
Transmit buffered ECG, vitals trend, and onset timestamp directly to Mission Control / Flight Surgeon.
why_this_happens: Long-duration spaceflight alters cardiac loading, autonomic balance, and electrolyte shifts; chest pain requires immediate rule-out of arrhythmia, ischemia, or pericardial irritation.
when_to_escalate: Always escalate immediately on any unexplained chest pressure, resting HR > 115 bpm with symptoms, SpO2 < 92%, or ECG abnormality.
disclaimer: Simulated protocol for demo. Real procedures come from the flight surgeon.

title: Injury / Bleeding in Microgravity
first_screen_message: Apply direct firm pressure with sterile gauze and contain fluids immediately using absorbent microgravity wound sleeves.
steps: Don nitrile gloves and eye protection to prevent free-floating fluid droplets.
Apply direct continuous pressure over the wound with sterile hemostatic gauze; anchor both patient and responder.
Once bleeding slows, enclose the area in a transparent containment sleeve and clean skin before dressing.
Record resting heart rate, blood pressure, and temperature to watch for shock or early wound infection.
Log mechanism of injury, time of hemostasis, and wound photo for Flight Surgeon review.
why_this_happens: In microgravity, blood pools into domes and floats off surfaces if disturbed; delayed immune healing in space increases infection risk if wounds are not cleanly sealed.
when_to_escalate: Escalate immediately if arterial/pulsing bleeding continues after 5 minutes of pressure, wound requires sutures, or signs of shock (HR rising, BP falling) develop.
disclaimer: Simulated protocol for demo. Real procedures come from the flight surgeon.

title: Severe Rash or Fever (Possible Viral Reactivation)
first_screen_message: Isolate skin lesions under sterile occlusive dressing, measure oral/tympanic temperature, and collect a saliva sample kit.
steps: Measure temperature twice (verify sensor contact) and record resting HR + HRV vs personal baseline.
Inspect skin for grouped vesicles, dermatomal rash (shingles/HSV-1/VZV), or cold sores; photograph and cover lesions to avoid viral shedding in cabin air.
Collect a saliva swab sample per kit instructions and store in the chilled sample slot.
Avoid touching eyes after touching lesions; sanitize shared crew surfaces and headset microphones.
Start crew quarantine/droplet precautions from 38.0 °C or if the rash is spreading (escalation starts at 38.3 °C, below).
why_this_happens: High stress, sleep deficiency, and EVA workload suppress T-cell immunity, triggering reactivation of latent herpesviruses (HSV-1, EBV, VZV) documented on ISS missions.
when_to_escalate: Escalate immediately if temperature ≥ 38.3 °C, rash involves the eye/face, fever persists > 24 h, or resting HR stays ≥ 2 SD above baseline.
disclaimer: Simulated protocol for demo. Real procedures come from the flight surgeon.

title: Breathing Difficulty / Cabin Air Check
first_screen_message: Check pulse oximeter (SpO2) and cabin CO2 ppm immediately; move crew to ventilated module and prepare supplemental O2 if SpO2 < 92%.
steps: Check cabin partial pressure of O2 and CO2 (target CO2 < 2,000 ppm; watch for > 3,000 ppm pockets in stagnant corners).
Measure SpO2 with a warmed finger clip and record respiratory rate and resting heart rate.
Seat or strap crew member upright/neutral in a module with strong airflow near a supply diffuser.
Check for wheezing, chemical/smoke odor, choking, or fever; administer emergency O2 mask if trained and SpO2 < 92%.
If CO2 pocket suspected, switch on auxiliary circulation fans and inspect CDRA scrubber status.
why_this_happens: In microgravity, exhaled CO2 forms localized pockets without fans, causing headaches and air hunger; smoke, ammonia, or respiratory infection can also drop SpO2 rapidly.
when_to_escalate: Escalate immediately if SpO2 < 92%, crew member cannot speak full sentences, cabin CO2 exceeds emergency threshold, or toxic leak is suspected.
disclaimer: Simulated protocol for demo. Real procedures come from the flight surgeon.
